research_question: In adults with heart disease, what is the effect of home-based cardiac rehabilitation (including digital/telehealth-supported programmes) versus supervised centre-based cardiac rehabilitation on triglycerides at 3–12 months follow-up?
outcome_description: Triglyceride levels measured in mmol/L (or converted to mmol/L) at the latest eligible follow-up between 3 and 12 months post-randomisation (reported as absolute follow-up or change from baseline).
positive_direction: Higher triglyceride levels in the home-based cardiac rehabilitation group compared to the centre-based cardiac rehabilitation group.
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials of adults with heart disease comparing home-based cardiac rehabilitation (including digital or telehealth-supported interventions) to supervised centre-based cardiac rehabilitation.
Studies reporting quantitative triglyceride measurements (as absolute follow-up values or change from baseline) at 3 to 12 months follow-up.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomized controlled trial (e.g., systematic reviews, meta-analyses, study protocols, editorials, observational or non-randomized studies).
Control arm does not consist of supervised centre-based cardiac rehabilitation (e.g., usual care, waitlist, community unsupervised, or no intervention comparators).
No quantitative data available on serum or plasma triglycerides allowing calculation/estimation of mean, SD, and sample size at 3–12 months follow-up.
Completely unrelated to cardiac rehabilitation in adults with cardiovascular disease.
moderators_to_extract: Home CR delivery mode (digital/telehealth-delivered vs traditional/paper/manual-based)
Follow-up timepoint within 3–12 months (e.g., 3 months, 6 months, 12 months)
Data type reported (post-intervention follow-up score vs change-from-baseline score)
Primary cardiac diagnosis (e.g., post-myocardial infarction, post-revascularisation, mixed CAD/heart failure)
Participant mean age and proportion of female participants
effect_size_note: Triglyceride levels reported in mg/dL should be converted to mmol/L using the standard conversion factor (mg/dL * 0.01129 = mmol/L, or mg/dL / 88.57). Either post-intervention values or change-from-baseline values are acceptable. If medians and IQRs/ranges are reported, mean and SD are approximated using Wan et al. (2014). For multi-arm trials with multiple eligible home-based arms, each home-based arm is compared against the shared centre-based control arm.
